title: Wicked: For Good
synopsis: Glinda has the crown. Elphaba has the price on her head. You're a school friend from Shiz who knows both of them. You can save one. Maybe.

nodes.text: A poster on every wall: 'Bring her in, alive or otherwise.' Elphaba's face is on it. So is your old roommate's. Glinda's broadcast plays softly from a megaphone — kind voice, terrible message. “Go to Glinda first” opens the route to The Emerald Palace. “Go to Elphaba first” changes the terms and carries you toward The Forest.

choices.text: Go to Glinda first
choices.consequence: Begin where you can still walk in. You choose to go to Glinda first. By The Emerald Palace, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Go to Elphaba first
choices.consequence: Begin where it's dangerous. You go to Elphaba first. The path to The Forest opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Glinda is, somehow, both glittering and tired. She lights up at you the way she always did. 'You're here,' she says. 'Don't tell me I shouldn't be doing this. The paths divide here: “Listen first before you advise” leads into The Animal Rebellion, while “Tell her this is wrong” makes The Wizard, Old the next reckoning.

choices.text: Listen first before you advise
choices.consequence: Hear her version of why. You commit to listen first before you advise. It carries you toward The Animal Rebellion, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Tell her this is wrong
choices.consequence: You commit to tell her this is wrong. It carries you toward The Wizard, Old, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You find Elphaba by following a trail no map shows — a kindness her broom leaves for those who knew her. She is thinner. The broom hovers beside her, mildly protective. The paths divide here: “Ask if she still trusts Glinda” leads into The Animal Rebellion, while “Tell her you came to help” makes The Wizard, Old the next reckoning.

nodes.text: A council of Animals — Goats, Bears, a wise old Cat — meets in a cave. They are organized in a way Oz has not seen in years. They want a public ally. Elphaba thinks that ally should be Glinda.

choices.text: Carry the message to Glinda
choices.consequence: You commit to carry the message to Glinda. It carries you toward Madame Morrible, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Press Elphaba to lead them publicly herself
choices.consequence: You commit to press Elphaba to lead them publicly herself. It carries you toward Fiyero, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You sneak into the Wizard's private quarters. He is older than the poster art, smaller, drinking. 'I'm not the villain,' he says. 'I'm just a man who scaled badly.' He may be telling the truth. He may be drunk.

choices.text: Press him on the Animal cages
choices.consequence: Truth from the throne first. You press him on the Animal cages. The path to Madame Morrible opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Get him to confess on a phonograph
choices.consequence: Evidence is the new sword. You choose to get him to confess on a phonograph. By Fiyero, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Glinda's chief adviser was your favorite teacher and is, you now see, the actual villain. She compliments your hair. She drops, casually, that she knows where your parents live. “Refuse to be intimidated” opens the route to The Trial in the Square. “Play dumb and gather information” changes the terms and carries you toward Glinda's Private Doubt.

nodes.text: Fiyero is alive — disguised, scarred, in the rebellion. He thought he'd never see you. He hugs you with both arms still working. He is, somehow, less of a prince now and more of a person.

choices.consequence: You choose to ask after Elphaba's plan. By The Trial in the Square, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The Wizard's regime holds public 'trials' of Animals every Tuesday. You and Fiyero, in the crowd, watch a Goat be sentenced for the crime of speaking. The crowd is mostly silent. A few cry. None move.

choices.text: Move first to disrupt
choices.consequence: You choose to move first to disrupt. By The Plan, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Document and leak it broadly instead
choices.consequence: Make the silent crowd reachable. You document and leak it broadly instead. The path to The Spell Book opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Glinda, alone, lets the act drop in front of you. She knows what she's enabled. She does not know how to undo it without dismantling herself. “Help her plan a public reversal” opens the route to The Plan. “Help her plan a quiet abdication” changes the terms and carries you toward The Spell Book.

nodes.text: Three nights: an Animals' march, a Glinda statement, a Wizard ambush. You and Fiyero and Elphaba and (terrifyingly) Glinda map it out on a stolen schoolroom blackboard. The chalk feels like Shiz. To choose “Run the plan as drafted” means meeting The March; “Insert a contingency for Glinda's safety” sends you toward The Bucket instead.

nodes.text: Elphaba pulls out the Grimmerie. There is a spell for unwriting the most powerful enchantment in Oz — but the cost is paid in something the caster loves. She looks at you for a long moment.

choices.text: Refuse to let her pay
choices.consequence: You choose to refuse to let her pay. By The March, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Animals fill the Yellow Brick Road with a quiet roar. Glinda steps forward, in pink, and reads a statement that detonates the regime's narrative in one paragraph. Madame Morrible's smile drops for the first time in your life.

choices.text: Stand visibly beside Glinda
choices.consequence: You commit to stand visibly beside Glinda. It carries you toward Madame Morrible's Storm, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Stay close to Elphaba and her broom
choices.consequence: Protect the most hunted. You commit to stay close to Elphaba and her broom. It carries you toward The Wizard's Surrender, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: An assassin's water bucket — actually a clever propagandist's prop — is meant to look like Elphaba melted. The plan: faked death, real escape. Elphaba, exhausted, considers it. Choose “Run the bucket plan” and Madame Morrible's Storm comes into view; choose “Convince her to stay and fight publicly” and the road bends toward The Wizard's Surrender.

nodes.text: Morrible calls a hurricane. You realize she has always been the one driving the weather. The sky goes the wrong color. The plan begins to come apart in front of you. “Use the Grimmerie to break her hold on the sky” opens the route to Elphaba, Public. “Get Glinda to publicly fire her in the storm” changes the terms and carries you toward The Forest Wedding.

nodes.text: The Wizard, watching from a balcony, sees the crowd and the plan and the storm and, almost gratefully, takes off the great hat. 'I'm done,' he says into the mic. 'I'm just a man.' Glinda looks at you. So does Elphaba. The plan, suddenly, has a new ending.

choices.text: Replace him with a council, not a queen
choices.consequence: You replace him with a council, not a queen. The path to Elphaba, Public opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Elphaba steps onto the palace balcony for the first time in years. The crowd, knowing the truth now, does not throw water. They throw flowers. Glinda is beside her holding her hand like they're in school again.

choices.text: Let Elphaba speak first
choices.consequence: Honor the woman who carried the hate. You let Elphaba speak first. The path to Two Friends opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Let Glinda speak first
choices.consequence: Honor the woman who carried the deception. You commit to let Glinda speak first. It carries you toward The Future of Oz, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Elphaba and Fiyero marry under a tree in the woods, the Animals as witnesses, Glinda in pink she's clearly made herself. You catch the bouquet by accident. Everyone laughs. The distance between Defying Gravity, Together and Schoolroom begins with the choice between “Stay for a long, quiet year” and “Go home to your village to teach.”

choices.consequence: Some weddings deserve a celebration that lasts. You choose to stay for a long, quiet year. By Defying Gravity, Together, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Go home to your village to teach

nodes.text: Glinda and Elphaba, you realize, never stopped being who they were at Shiz. The world bent them in opposite directions and yet — somehow — they still finish each other's harmonies. You smile from the wings. “Take the post they offer you in the new council” draws you toward The New Oz; “Take the smaller post in a province they trust to you” leaves Munchkin County waiting on the other side.

choices.consequence: Put your shoulder to the work. You choose to take the post they offer you in the new council. By The New Oz, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.consequence: You choose to take the smaller post in a province they trust to you. By Munchkin County, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: A council forms — Animals and humans, witches and ordinary citizens. It is imperfect. It is real. Glinda holds the gavel. Elphaba flies between provinces, an emissary nobody calls a fugitive anymore. The road still runs toward Yellow Brick, Repaved. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Help draft Oz's first constitution” and choosing “Take a long, quiet sabbatical.”

choices.text: Help draft Oz's first constitution
choices.consequence: Words can also save countries. You help draft Oz's first constitution. The path to Yellow Brick, Repaved opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Crews lay new brick over a road that once led to a fraud. Children skip beside the workers. You stand at a window and decide whether your next year is a desk in the capital or a long walk through provinces you've never seen.

choices.text: Take the desk and write the words
choices.consequence: You commit to take the desk and write the words. It carries you toward The New Oz, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Take the walk and let others write
choices.consequence: The road, the longer way. You take the walk and let others write. The path to Sabbatical opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Years later you watch Elphaba and Glinda fly between provinces on the same broom, both laughing, both lecturing each other about leadership. Some friendships outlast the worst chapters of a country. The road into Defying Gravity, Together began with “Stay for a long, quiet year” in The Forest Wedding; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You teach in the village school. You tell the children a version of events that is mostly true and entirely useful. They draw Glinda in pink and Elphaba in green and both of them as friends. They learn that's allowed.

The constitution you helped draft outlives all of you. The Wicked Witch, in history class, becomes a hero. Madame Morrible becomes a villain. Glinda becomes a complicated figure — which is exactly what she always wanted.

You become a quiet, beloved governor of a small province. You set up an Animals' school and a council of elders that meets weekly for tea. Elphaba and Glinda visit every Yule. The province survives them both. You sleep well.
You take a year and walk Oz on foot. You meet people who only know the story as gossip. You realize history is in the hands of whoever writes the songs. You write a few. They survive. So do you.
